briefing.text: The hypothesis names oesophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC). Check CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED / ONCOTREE_CODE in data_clinical_sample.txt to see whether this cohort is EAC. If it is, the claim is about this study, and under the benchmark convention 'Not verifiable' is the wrong kind of label, even though the MAF may have no trinucleotide-context column. Reconstruct the flanking bases where you can (for example from the Codons / codon-change or reference-sequence fields), look at the overall A>C/T>G spectrum, and fall back on established biology where the data cannot test the claim directly.
briefing.reason: A missing context column could push the team toward a wrong 'Not verifiable'. The label convention makes deciding the cohort's identity the first step.

briefing.text: AA/TT dinucleotides are very common in the exome, so a raw count of A>C at AA is not evidence of a signature. Measure enrichment against a background. For example, compare the share of strand-collapsed T>G SNVs that have a flanking T with the same share for the other T>N substitutions in the same samples, or with the background ApA/TpT frequency, using a Fisher or binomial test. Also check that the result is not driven by a few hypermutated samples.
briefing.reason: This determines whether the spectrum analysis can show a signature at all, rather than just reflecting how common the sequence context is.

briefing.text: A>C at AA and T>G at TT are the same mutation class read on opposite strands. COSMIC SBS uses pyrimidine-collapsed notation, so A>C is reported as T>G. Collapse the MAF's Reference_Allele/Tumor_Seq_Allele2 to the pyrimidine strand and reverse-complement the flanking context with it.
briefing.reason: If strand is handled inconsistently, the enrichment is undercounted or miscounted.

briefing.text: Background biology: in the EAC literature, T>G (A>C) transversions at TT/AA, with a CTT peak (COSMIC SBS17a/b), are described as a characteristic mutational process of oesophageal adenocarcinoma, linked to acid/oxidative damage (8-oxo-dGTP). They are reported as an unusually large share of substitutions compared with other tumour types. Use this as the reference point when you interpret the cohort's spectrum, and when the data alone are ambiguous.
briefing.reason: The label convention says to use established biology where the tables cannot test a claim directly, so the team needs the relevant prior.

shared_assumptions: Both teams took neighbouring bases only from VEP codon strings, so the context test covers only flanks inside coding codons. Neither checked whether the 81%-vs-42% 3'T gap could come from codon or amino-acid composition rather than from mutation preference.
Both treated pooled SNVs as independent records and used Fisher tests. Neither checked whether a few T>G-heavy samples (up to 47% per sample) drive the context enrichment.

Both counted every sample in the MAF as EAC. The sample table has 151 rows, but only 146 tumour barcodes appear in the MAF. PRIMARY_SITE_OTHER splits into Esophagus (54), Cardia/GEJ (41) and blank (55).
unused_evidence: Non-coding SNVs (Intron 2271, 3'UTR 1083, RNA 1145, IGR/Flank, about 5k rows) have no codon string, so neither team's context test used them. Genome_Change and HGVSc give a position but no flank, so the context for these rows is still untested.
PRIMARY_SITE_OTHER (Esophagus vs Cardia/GEJ) and BARRETTS_ESOPHAGUS. Neither team checked whether the signal holds within the strictly oesophageal tumours.
Team A did not use t_alt_count/Allelic_fraction or the Matched/Unmatched status (SOMATIC_STATUS) to rule out germline or artefact T>G calls. Team B did a Matched/Unmatched split but no VAF filter.
unresolved_weak_points: Both named codon-only context as their weakest point. Both stratified by codon position, but neither built a null model: the same expected-context calculation applied to random or permuted substitutions within the same codons. So the bias was reported and only partly resolved.
Team B's first record reported enrichment for a 5' C (CTT/AAG, 60% vs 44%). Its later record reports a 3' T. The two orientations were not reconciled in writing.
Team A's silent-only stratum showed 0/73. It was dismissed as a genetic-code artefact without a direct test.
second_readings: 'A>C at AA' could mean the mutated A has its A neighbour on either side (5' or 3'). After strand collapsing that is T>G with a 3' T or with a 5' T. Team A found no 5' T enrichment, so the reading of the claim affects how strong the evidence is.

'Mutational signature' could mean an extracted signature (NMF/SBS17-like) and not only an enriched class share. The label convention, though, ties the answer to the source study's reported finding, which both teams treat as reporting the signature as present.
challenge.verdict: I trust the agreed 'False' fairly well. Both teams found a sizeable T>G (A>C) share and a strong T>G-specific 3'T enrichment in an EAC cohort, and this fits established EAC biology (SBS17-like). The remaining risk is that the context comes from codon strings with no explicit null, but the T>C/T>A internal controls make a pure artefact unlikely.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Build a null for the codon-derived 3'T share: for each observed T>G, compute the 3'T share expected from all T positions in the same codon set (or permute substitution types within codon position). Is the observed T>G 3'T share still clearly above that null, and does this change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Recompute the 3'T enrichment per sample, or with sample-level resampling, rather than with a pooled Fisher test. In what fraction of samples with at least 10 T>G calls does the enrichment hold, and does this change your inference?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Repeat the T>G share and context test after restricting to PRIMARY_SITE_OTHER == Esophagus and to calls with Allelic_fraction above a minimum threshold. Does either restriction change the result or your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your first record reports 5' C enrichment (CTT/AAG) and your later one 3' T enrichment. Tabulate the full trinucleotide (5' and 3' together) for coding T>G against T>C/T>A in one table. Are the two findings the same context, and does this change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Compute the 3'T share expected under a null that uses the same codon positions and reference codons (e.g. permuted substitution classes). Is the 81% vs 41-43% gap still present beyond codon-composition effects, and does this change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Check the context-enrichment result per sample and after excluding the samples with the highest T>G share, and separately within Esophagus vs Cardia/GEJ tumours. Does the enrichment persist, and does any of this change your method?

findings.question: When the trinucleotide context of coding SNVs can be reconstructed only from the codon strings in a VEP-annotated MAF (no reference genome), what is the accepted way to correct for codon-composition bias when testing whether one substitution class is enriched for a given neighbouring base?
findings.answer: NOT WEB-VERIFIED: the research gateway returned HTTP 403 on every call, so this comes from background knowledge. Use an opportunity-normalised null. Stratify by codon position, because only neighbours inside the codon are visible: position-3 sites have no 3' neighbour and position-1 sites have no 5' neighbour. Within each stratum, estimate the expected neighbour-base frequency for the same reference base from the coding sequence. One way is to use all reference codons of coding SNVs, or the codon/trinucleotide opportunity of the exome, as deconstructSigs exome2genome-style tri.counts do. Then test the observed neighbour fraction of the class against that expectation with a binomial or chi-square test. Alternatively, run a permutation test that shuffles substitution class within reference base, codon position and strand. Comparing with other substitution classes from the same reference base works as an internal control, but it is not a full null on its own, since those classes have their own context preferences. The best fix is to fetch real flanks from a reference FASTA, but none is available here.

findings.question: In COSMIC SBS17a/SBS17b, which flanking position (5' or 3') carries the characteristic T in the pyrimidine-strand T>G context, and how does that map onto 'A>C at AA' notation on the purine strand?
findings.answer: NOT WEB-VERIFIED: the research gateway returned HTTP 403, so this comes from background knowledge. The characteristic T is the 3' flank. SBS17b peaks at T>G, and SBS17a at T>C, in CTT, TTT, ATT and GTT contexts, i.e. N[T>G]T. Reverse-complemented onto the purine strand this is A[A>C]N: the mutated A has a 5' A, which forms the 'AA' dinucleotide. On a pyrimidine-collapsed spectrum, team A's result ('3' T enriched, 5' T not') is the SBS17-consistent pattern and fits the claim of A>C at AA as worded.
